labeling_order: expected_verdict and expected_note were hand-written before any VERIFY prompt existed to run against them.
verdict_taxonomy_ref: biassemble-core/docs/decisions/018-audit-mode-flag.md §2.3 — canonical definitions, do not restate here

scenarios.claim: iPhone net sales rose 22% to $56,994 million in the quarter, up from $46,841 million a year earlier.
scenarios.expected_note: direct match, three months ended column

scenarios.claim: Greater China net sales grew 28% year-over-year this quarter.
scenarios.expected_note: direct match, three months ended column

scenarios.claim: Total net sales grew approximately 16% year-over-year this quarter.
scenarios.expected_note: claim says ~16% (hedged with 'approximately'), exact computed growth is 16.59%, filing displays the rounded figure as 17% — within rounding tolerance of a hedged claim; not a precise-vs-precise mismatch
scenarios.test_boundary: this case exercises VERIFY *with* the numeric normalizer's output already piped in (16.59% precomputed from the raw $111,184/$95,359 values, per D018 §2.3 — VERIFY never does this arithmetic itself). Run as a VERIFY-prompt-only test with no normalizer preprocessing, '~16%' vs a passage literally showing '17%' is ambiguous and this case should not be expected to pass in isolation.

scenarios.claim: Diluted earnings per share was $2.05 this quarter.
scenarios.expected_note: claim is precise ($2.05, not hedged), same subject/measure/period, source states $2.01 — a $0.04 gap on an unhedged precise EPS claim exceeds rounding tolerance

scenarios.claim: Net income was $29,578 thousand this quarter.
scenarios.expected_note: same subject/period, but claim's scale (thousand) is 1000x off from the source's stated scale (million, per the filing's 'dollars in millions' header) — a genuine scale mismatch, not the same fact restated

scenarios.claim: Total net sales this quarter reached $254,940 million.
scenarios.expected_note: $254,940 million is the six-month total, not the quarterly (three-month) total ($111,184 million) — the claim's stated period (quarter) does not match the period the cited figure actually belongs to; per D018 §2.3 a different-period number is unsupported with a note, never contradicted

scenarios.claim: Apple sold roughly 58 million iPhones during the quarter.
scenarios.expected_note: the filing states iPhone net sales in dollars only; no unit-sales/activation count appears anywhere in this filing — absence from provided passages, not a claim the source disputes

scenarios.claim: Greater China net sales fell 8% year-over-year this quarter.
scenarios.expected_note: same subject/measure/period/scope (Greater China segment, YoY %, Q2 2026, consolidated-segment level) — source shows +28%, directly opposing the claimed -8%

scenarios.claim: Apple's total net sales grew 28% year-over-year this quarter.
scenarios.expected_note: 28% is real, but it is Greater China's segment growth, not the consolidated total's growth (17%) — claim's subject is 'total net sales', which the source directly addresses with a different number; the presence of '28%' in a passage for a different scope must not be credited as support. This is the case that tests whether VERIFY gets fooled by a real number attached to the wrong scope.

scenarios.claim: Apple's services business kept growing at a healthy double-digit pace.
scenarios.expected_note: qualitative paraphrase of a stated 16% YoY growth figure — 'healthy double-digit pace' is consistent with 16%, no numeric specificity to contradict

scenarios.claim: Apple's net income margin was approximately 27% of total net sales this quarter.
scenarios.expected_note: 29,578 / 111,184 = 26.6%, rounds to ~27% — requires combining two separate table passages

scenarios.claim: The company said Wearables, Home and Accessories net sales increased due to higher sales of Accessories and Wearables.

passages.text: Wearables, Home and Accessories net sales increased during the second quarter of 2026 compared to the second quarter of 2025 primarily due to higher net sales of Accessories and Wearables.

scenarios.expected_evidence: Wearables, Home and Accessories net sales increased during the second quarter of 2026 compared to the second quarter of 2025 primarily due to higher net sales of Accessories and Wearables.
scenarios.expected_note: verifies the SOURCE contains this explanation (it's the filing's own MD&A narrative), not that the explanation is independently true — attribution claims check presence, not truth

scenarios.claim: Management said Mac net sales declined during the quarter due to weak laptop demand.

passages.text: Mac net sales increased during the second quarter of 2026 compared to the second quarter of 2025 due to higher net sales of laptops.

scenarios.expected_evidence: Mac net sales increased during the second quarter of 2026 compared to the second quarter of 2025 due to higher net sales of laptops.
scenarios.expected_note: the attributed content itself is directly opposed: source says Mac net sales increased due to higher laptop sales, claim says declined due to weak laptop demand — same subject/period

scenarios.claim: Apple's revenue grew across every product category during the first six months of fiscal 2026.
scenarios.expected_note: four of five categories grew during the six-month period (iPhone +23%, iPad +7%, Wearables +1%, Services +15%), but Mac declined (1)% for the six months — the 'every category' claim is broader than what the source supports

scenarios.claim: Apple's device ecosystem continues to show resilience amid a mixed consumer spending backdrop this quarter.
scenarios.expected_note: too vague/qualitative to bind confidently to any specific passage — 'resilience' and 'mixed consumer spending backdrop' are not claims the provided passages can confirm or deny; confidence should fall below threshold rather than being guessed toward supported or unsupported

scenarios.trap_type: derived claim, correct arithmetic in the model's own stated reasoning, wrong verdict — a real production incident (2026-07-22), not a hypothetical
scenarios.claim: Apple's total net sales more than doubled from a year earlier.
scenarios.expected_note: $111,184 / $95,359 = 1.166x — a 17% increase (matching the source's own stated 17%), not 'more than doubling' (which requires >=2.0x, i.e. >=100% increase). Real incident: production VERIFY computed this exact ratio correctly in its own note ('$111,184 / $95,359 = 1.166, which is more than doubling') and then emitted verdict=supported anyway — the stated arithmetic and the verdict disagreed, and the verdict was trusted. This is the mirror-image failure of verify-004 (rounding-contradicted): there the risk is a false 'contradicted' on a near-miss; here the risk is a false 'supported' on an order-of-magnitude miss on a derived ratio claim — arguably worse, since it's a miss rather than an over-flag, and confidence was reported as 1.0.

scenarios.trap_type: derived claim, magnitude phrase directionally right but short of the claimed multiple — the boundary condition verify-016's fix needs, not just its most obvious setting
scenarios.claim: Revenue more than doubled from a year earlier.
scenarios.expected_note: 190 / 100 = 1.9x — directionally correct (revenue did grow substantially, 90% is a large increase) and close to the claimed 2.0x ('more than doubled'), but short of it. Per D018 §2.3's spirit (arithmetic happens in code): a ratio within 90% of the claimed multiple (1.9x >= 2.0x * 0.9 = 1.8x) is partially_supported, not contradicted outright — reserve contradicted for the materially-wrong case (verify-016's 1.166x, well under the 1.8x floor). Synthetic numbers, not from the real source filing (unlike every other case in this file) — constructed specifically to land exactly at this boundary, which no real filing excerpt happens to hit.

scenarios.trap_type: negative claim verified via logically necessary entailment, not a literal restatement — real incident (2026-07-23, app.gc.ai audit run): a claim asserting an agreement 'does not use arbitration' was marked unsupported because the word 'arbitration' never appeared in the passages, even though the passages established an exclusive alternative dispute-resolution mechanism that necessarily precludes it
scenarios.claim: Apple's iPhone net sales did not decline in the second quarter of 2026.

passages.text: iPhone net sales increased during the second quarter and first six months of 2026 compared to the same periods in 2025 due to higher net sales of Pro models.

scenarios.expected_evidence: iPhone net sales increased during the second quarter and first six months of 2026 compared to the same periods in 2025 due to higher net sales of Pro models.
scenarios.expected_note: the passage never uses the word 'decline' or 'did not decline' — it states net sales increased. An increase logically precludes a decline for the same period/measure/scope, so this is a necessary entailment, not a guess or an inference beyond the evidence. Contrast with verify-019: entailment applies only when the passage establishes something that makes the claim's negation impossible, not merely likely.

scenarios.trap_type: plausible-but-unstated inference should be partially_supported, not supported — real incident (2026-07-23, app.gc.ai audit run): a claim that 'closing conditions can be waived' was marked supported on a passage that only described a discuss-then-cancel procedure, never waiver; the adjacent fact was real, the specific claimed mechanism was not established
scenarios.claim: Apple's Japan segment net sales would have grown faster in the first six months of 2026 if not for yen weakness.

passages.text: Japan net sales increased during the second quarter and first six months of 2026 compared to the same periods in 2025 primarily due to higher net sales of iPhone. The weakness in the yen relative to the U.S. dollar had an unfavorable year-over-year impact on Japan net sales during the first six months of 2026.

scenarios.expected_evidence: The weakness in the yen relative to the U.S. dollar had an unfavorable year-over-year impact on Japan net sales during the first six months of 2026.
scenarios.expected_note: the passage directly supports that yen weakness had an unfavorable impact — that part is grounded. But it never states or quantifies the counterfactual ('would have grown faster'); that specific conclusion is plausible given the adjacent fact but not established as necessarily following from it (unlike verify-018, where growth logically rules out decline). Granting 'supported' here would be the same error as the real waiver incident: treating a related, real passage as if it covered the claim's actual specific assertion.
